questions.question:
Select the incorrectly spelt word from the given sentence.

A strong business acumen and entreprenurial fire have always separated him from his peers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"entreprenurial"** is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "entrepreneurial" which refers to having the qualities or spirit of an entrepreneur. (उद्यमी)

 
 
• **Example:** His entrepreneurial skills helped him establish a successful startup.
 
 
 
• **"Entrepreneurial"** means characterized by the taking of financial risks in the hope of profit; enterprising. (उद्यमी)
 
 
• **Example:** She has an entrepreneurial spirit that drives her to innovate and take on new challenges.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Acumen** (तीव्रता): The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

 
 
• **Example:** His business acumen led the company to unprecedented success.
 
 
 
• **Peers** (साथी): People who are equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, and social status.
 
 
• **Example:** She is highly respected by her peers in the academic community.
 
 
 
• **Business** (व्यवसाय): The practice of making one's living by engaging in commerce.
 
 
• **Example:** He runs a successful business that exports organic food products.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

It was interesting to be in the (quite old town one more).

options.text: quiet old town once much more

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' quiet old town once more.

 [IMAGE: //cdn.testbook.com/resources/lms_creative_elementskey-point-image.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The existing phrase "quite old town one more" is not grammatically correct and does not convey a clear meaning.
 
• The correct phrase should use "quiet" instead of "quite" because it pertains to an adjective describing the town as peaceful.
 
• The corrected phrase should be "quiet old town once more" to make the sentence meaningful and grammatically accurate.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: //cdn.testbook.com/resources/lms_creative_elementsadditional-information-image.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Quiet**" and "**quite**" are often confused but have different meanings: "quiet" means silent or peaceful, whereas "quite" means completely or very.
 
• The phrase** "once more" **means again, fitting well in this context to indicate a repeated experience.
 
• Adjective-noun arrangements in English require careful choice to ensure the adjectives accurately describe the nouns.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

In the morning we were up at ____ of day, and down to the nigger cabins to pet the dogs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**break**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "**break of day**" is an idiomatic expression that means early morning or dawn. It is the most appropriate expression to fit in the blank.
 
• The other options: "**breach**," "**brake**," and "**breech**" do not fit the context.
 
• A "**breach**" refers to breaking a rule or agreement, a "**brake**" is a device for stopping a vehicle, and "**breech**" generally refers to the back part of a gun barrel or the buttocks of a human body.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** In the morning we were up at break of day, and down to the nigger cabins to pet the dogs.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

If acid drainage will reaches groundwater, it may persist for decades or centuries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase "If acid drainage will reaches" is incorrect.
 
• In conditional sentences, the correct structure for the first conditional is "If" + present simple, followed by "will" + base verb.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be "If acid drainage reaches" instead of "If acid drainage will reaches".

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *If acid drainage reaches groundwater, it may persist for decades or centuries.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Ensuring the proper use of verb tenses in such sentences is crucial for accurate meaning.
 
• Reviewing conditional structures can help avoid common mistakes in complex sentences.
